doc_verification.detail: Documentation reachable (api.qdrant.tech), version 1.19.x matches target v1.18.2. Documentation specifies delete endpoint exists but does NOT explicitly state expected behavior for deleting already-deleted collections. Behavioral contract qdrant_behavioral_delete_invisibility_001 from structured_contract.json states 'get collection returns 404' after delete, but does not specify idempotency behavior for re-delete operations.

secondary_observations: Second delete on already-deleted collection returned status 200 with result:false

http_semantics.note: Second delete returned HTTP 200 with body {"result":false,"status":"ok"} - client error (deleting non-existent collection) returned as 2xx success status, distinguishing by result:false vs result:true

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: Deleted collection should not be visible in get collection and list collections; scenario: Delete collection -> get collection -> collection not in list; expected_behavior: get collection returns 404, list collections does not include deleted collection
contract_grounding.note: Contract specifies POST-DELETE visibility (get returns 404) but does not specify RE-DELETE behavior. However, accepting re-delete with 200+result:false violates idempotency expectation - deleted collection should return 404 if it doesn't exist.

chain_links: script:semantic_collections_delete_004.py (first delete, then second delete on same collection)

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: API Handler (collections_api.rs:160-178) calls dispatcher.submit_collection_meta_op(DeleteCollectionOperation) -> TableOfContent.perform_collection_meta_op (collection_meta_ops.rs:78-81) calls self.delete_collection (collection_meta_ops.rs:215-300) -> Returns Ok(bool) where bool=true if deleted, bool=false if not found -> process_response (helpers.rs:80-89) converts Ok(bool) to HTTP 200 with ApiResponse {result: Some(bool), status: Ok} -> No StorageError::NotFound is ever thrown for missing collection

mundane_explanation.surviving: State logic violation confirmed - deleting already-deleted collection returns success (200 OK) instead of expected 404 Not Found or error. Source code analysis reveals this is BY-DESIGN idempotency: the delete_collection handler deliberately returns Ok(false) (HTTP 200 with result:false) when collection is not found, rather than throwing StorageError::NotFound which would map to HTTP 404. The validate_collection_exists method exists but is NOT called before delete operation. This design allows idempotent delete operations but violates REST semantics where DELETE on non-existent resource should return 404.
